title: use clang-tools instead of clang-format (rolling) by dskkato · Pull Request #1865 · ros2/ros2 · GitHub
body_rendered_text:
Description


clang-tidy is missing in pixi environment. Since clang-tools contains both clang-format and clang-tidy, I suggest to use clang-tools instead of clang-format


Fixes #1864


Is this user-facing behavior change?


Yes. Uses can use clang-tidy in pixi environment.


Did you use Generative AI?


Assisted by CodeX, Luna.


Additional Information


clang-tools installs following packages/tools. The reason I didn't specify clang-tidy is that it is missing in conda-forge registry.



clang-tidy


clangd


clang-check


clang-query


clang-rename


clang-repl


clang-doc


clang-include-fixer


clang-include-cleaner


clang-apply-replacements


clang-change-namespace


clang-move


clang-reorder-fields


clang-scan-deps


scan-build


scan-view


run-clang-tidy


intercept-build


find-all-symbols


modularize


diagtool
discussion_rendered_text:
How is this kind of dependency maintenance backported to other distros?


I prepared the changes for the Lyrical version in #1866 as a draft PR, but let me know if this is handled automatically (e.g., by Mergify?) or if I should do something else.
we use Mergify semi-automatically: we tell it to create backport PRs when we think it's needed. We'll probably backport this to all distros that have a pixi.toml file.
Looks good on my end. This allows ament/ament_lint#563 (comment) to pass on Windows.
@mjcarroll @knmcguire any thoughts or objections about switching from clang-format instead of clang-tools and thus installing a lot more dependencies?

I think it is fine myself. The extra space the packages takes up is neglectable compared the space of building ROS itself
